To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HLP-2, but not HLP-6 binds to LPS, folds into β-strands, and self-assembles to form aggregates.
the bactericidal activity, the lag phase in killing, the LPS binding, and the structure of the peptides were strongly dependent on the presence of Met in the peptides.
the bactericidal activity and the lag phase of the synthetic lactoferrin peptide are due to a slow self-association process of the peptides at the outer membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and association of HLP-1 and HLP-2 with E. coli O111 and with LPS.
understanding the mechanism of action of HLP-1 and its synthetic analogues.
the structure and mechanism of antimicrobial activity of a lactoferrin-derived peptide, HLP- 2, against E. coli serotype O11.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HLP-2 has a higher affinity to LPS than HLP-6 and that this difference in affinity is responsible for the observed differences in antimicrobial activity.
HLP-2 is more efficient in destabilizing E. coli outer membranes and killing E. coli cells than HLP-6 due to a more efficient self-assembly at the bacterial surface.
HLP-2, but not HLP-6 (which lacks a Met residue), is a bactericidal peptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amphipathic nature of the peptide is essential for LPS binding but not for bactericidal activity.
HLP-2 is a potent antimicrobial peptide that binds and folds into a β-strand structure in the presence of LSP.
a peptide with an α-helical structure in solution is capable of folding into a β-structure upon interaction with LPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bactericidal activity is not only a function of the peptide-LPS interaction but is also related to the peptide-peptide interaction.
the structure of the peptides is crucial for the bactericidal activity.

a small change in the sequence of a lactoferrin-derived peptide, which does not alter the binding affinity for LPS, can dramatically change the mechanism of action of the peptide and the kinetics of its interaction with the target.
